### Workload
- Only template q16: partsupp JOIN part (filtered: brand<>, type NOT LIKE prefix, size IN 8 consts) + NOT IN (supplier LIKE) mark join, GROUP BY brand,type,size count(DISTINCT suppkey). ~27.8k groups, ~1.18M rows into the agg. Bench ~174-180 ms (noisy machine: the reference ranged 179-253 ms in E0002).
- Operator CPU in the profile: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.67 s, inner HASH_JOIN 0.37 s, partsupp scan with BF 0.28 s, supplier scan 0.09 s. Total CPU is about 1.44 s (8 threads x 180 ms).
- Join only with count(*): 82 ms wall. Adding the count(DISTINCT) agg: about +140 ms.

### KEY FINDING round 3: the distinct table's keys are near-unique
- GROUP BY brand,type,size,suppkey gives 1,184,608 groups from 1,184,892 rows. HASH_GROUP_BY alone is 0.84 s CPU.
- Each thread sinks about 150k rows, which is below ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD = 1M, so DecideAdaptation's SkipLookups (hll_pct > 0.95) never fires. The HT probes, inserts and abandons every 21845 rows while deduplicating nothing.
- R3 dispatched: "Early tentative SkipLookups for near-unique radix aggregate sinks". A reversible skip, checked at each Abandon (hll/sink > 0.95 and materialized/sink > 0.95).
- If it fails: check whether the sink is really on the wall critical path. Neither E0002 nor this has measured the wall time per phase (pipeline vs distinct finalize vs main sink vs main finalize).

### Round-2 facts (E0002 timers, CPU ms over 8 threads)
- distinct sink AddChunk ~253, Abandon ~40, MaybeRepartition ~100-146, distinct finalize Combine ~110-126, scan ~18, main-HT sink from the distinct scan ~176-190 (about 150 ns/row), main finalize ~30.
- E0002 fix (unpartitioned staging only for AllConstant layouts) cut about 110 ms CPU but gave only -0.6% wall (median about -5%, noisy). A good mechanism with a small wall effect. SkipLookups also bypasses staging, so E0003 subsumes it.

### Codebase facts
- Radix aggregate HT (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): with more than 2 threads the sink capacity is 32768 (resize threshold 21845). Abandon() is called in Sink when full. DecideAdaptation (line ~424) runs only at 1M rows per thread. MAXIMUM_FINAL_SINK_RADIX_BITS = 8.
- GroupedAggregateHashTable::SkipLookups (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:264) is just a flag. With skip on, FindOrCreateGroups (~line 685) appends straight to partitioned_data. count still increments, so abandons still happen.
- With radix_bits >= 3 and few new groups per chunk, new groups are staged in unpartitioned_data and repartitioned on Abandon.
- The count(DISTINCT) path is in physical_hash_aggregate.cpp. HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask::AggregateDistinctGrouping (~648-754) GetData's the distinct radix table and Sinks into the main table_data with a per-task local state. The number of tasks is min(MaxThreads, threads).
- Perfect HJ: CanDoPerfectHashJoin (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66) uses runtime min/max from the filter pushdown and MAX_BUILD_SIZE = 1048576, INNER only. CAVEAT: when perfect HJ is used, FinalizeFilters gets is_perfect_hashtable=true and CanUseBloomFilter likely refuses the BF. q16's partsupp scan would then lose its BF (8M rows down to 1.24M) and probe 8M rows. Any perfect-HJ widening must keep a probe-side filter, or it may regress.
- Compressed materialization: p_brand -> uhugeint, p_type (25 chars) stays VARCHAR, p_size -> utinyint.
- InClauseRewriter: IN lists with >= 6 constants become a MARK join.
- dbe-tool: no perf, and output piping into grep works. EXPLAIN ANALYZE variants are cheap bisection. Wrapping in count(*) can drop the distinct agg; use max(col).

### Experiments
- E0001 early HT grow (retired): ~3%. Abandon thrashing in the main table is small.
- E0002 skip unpartitioned staging for non-constant layouts (retired): -0.6% visible, -110 ms CPU measured.
- E0003 (R3) early SkipLookups: pending.

### Backlog ideas (ranked)
1. (dispatched R3) early SkipLookups.
2. The main-HT sink in the distinct finalize costs about 150 ns/row. Ideas: partition the distinct table by group-key hash only, so each partition finalizes its groups directly (big change), or presize the local main HT.
3. Perfect HJ for the sparse range (build 296k, range 2M). See the BF caveat above; needs a perfect-bitmap probe filter.
4. Enforce the IN-list filter in the scan instead of the mark join (small, 2-4%).

### Prior-run notes (other workloads, see MEMORY index): perfect HJ / large perfect HA gave ~20% on q13.

issues.title: Early tentative SkipLookups for near-unique radix aggregate sinks
issues.hypothesis: In q16 the count(DISTINCT) aggregate first sinks into a distinct radix table keyed on (brand, type, size, suppkey). Those keys are almost all unique. A plain GROUP BY on the same 4 keys returns 1,184,608 groups from 1,184,892 input rows, and its HASH_GROUP_BY alone takes 0.84 s CPU, more than the 0.67 s the whole distinct aggregate takes. Each of the 8 threads sees only about 150k rows. That is far below ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD = 1M, so DecideAdaptation (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424) never fires and the table never switches to SkipLookups, even though it has a hll_percentage > 0.95 rule written for exactly this case. So every row pays for the probe, key compare (on a VARCHAR key), HT insert and unpartitioned staging. Then about every 21845 rows the HT is Abandon()ed (32768 capacity), having deduplicated nothing. E0002 measured this sink at about 253 ms CPU for AddChunk, 40 ms for Abandon and 100-146 ms for MaybeRepartition/staging, about 400 ms of roughly 1.44 s total CPU. All of that dedup work is redone in the finalize Combine anyway. With SkipLookups the sink only hashes and appends straight to partitioned_data. That also bypasses the unpartitioned staging and repartition that E0002 found to be the VARCHAR-specific cost.
issues.plan: In src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp, RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink, at the point where `ht.Abandon()` is called (more than 2 threads, not external), add an early, reversible adaptation while `!lstate.adapted`. Right after the Abandon, compute sink_count = ht.GetSinkCount(), hll = MinValue(ht.GetHLLUpperBound(), sink_count) and materialized = ht.GetMaterializedCount(). If hll/sink_count > 0.95 AND materialized/sink_count > 0.95, call ht.SkipLookups(). The second test is the HT's actual dedup, so data with real duplicates inside one HT fill never triggers. Otherwise, if lookups are currently skipped, turn them back on. Add `void GroupedAggregateHashTable::SetSkipLookups(bool)`, or `EnableLookups()`, in src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp and src/include/duckdb/execution/aggregate_hashtable.hpp. Toggling right after Abandon is safe because the pointer table is cleared and count is 0. Keep the HLL enabled and leave `adapted` false, so the existing 1M-row DecideAdaptation still makes the final call. Optionally, when hll_pct exceeds 0.95 there, it keeps skip_lookups. When the data later turns duplicate-heavy, the re-check at the next abandon (each fill, about 21k rows) re-enables lookups. Do not touch the grow-strategy path (2 threads or fewer). Validate with q16, with a plain high-cardinality GROUP BY, and with a low-cardinality GROUP BY such as 25k groups over 10M rows, to confirm that one does not trigger. Using hash(p_type) in the query is a cheap way to bisect.
issues.expected_gain: q16 8-15%. It should remove most of the roughly 300-400 ms CPU of probe, abandon and staging work in the distinct-table sink. The finalize Combine sees the same row count as before, because the HT deduplicated nothing.
issues.generality: Any count(DISTINCT x) GROUP BY g, where (g, x) is near-unique, and any high-cardinality GROUP BY or DISTINCT with fewer than 1M rows per thread (about 8M total at 8 threads), the size where the existing adaptation never fires. Possible slowdowns: data whose first ~20k rows per thread are unique but which has many duplicates later. The per-fill HLL re-check bounds that to at most one fill of skipped dedup per transition.
issues.risk: Low to medium. SkipLookups is an existing, correctness-safe mode: the finalize always deduplicates. The main risk is a performance regression on data that is unique early and duplicated later, which the reversible check mitigates. HLL accuracy at about 20k rows is a few percent, so the 0.95 threshold has some margin.
